Hard rules: pure JavaScript for Node.js, ES Modules only (`import`/`export`, NEVER `require`/`module.exports`), ALL files must use the `.mjs` suffix, ZERO npm/external dependencies, imports only of local files and they MUST include the full `.mjs` suffix (e.g. `import { x } from './pyvalues.mjs'`), no embedding of Python. Create ONLY the files assigned to you below — other agents are creating the other files in parallel; do not create, modify, or even read their assigned files (they may not exist yet). When done, verify your files parse with `node --check <file>` and report what you created.

## Shared interface contract (already agreed by all agents — implement/consume EXACTLY this)

Module `/output/lib/pyvalues.mjs` exports:
- `class PyFloat` — wraps a JS number in `.value`; represents a Python float.
- `class PyTuple` — wraps a JS array in `.items`; represents a Python tuple.
- `class PyDict` — insertion-ordered Python dict. Constructor takes optional `entries` (array of `[key, value]` pairs; on duplicate keys the LAST value wins but the key keeps its FIRST-seen position). Methods: `set(k,v)`, `get(k)` (undefined if absent), `has(k)`, `keys()` (JS array of original key objects), `values()` (JS array), `items()` (JS array of `PyTuple`), `size` getter. Key equality must treat `true`/`1`, `false`/`0` as equal (Python semantics: bool IS int), and match numbers/PyFloats numerically (1 == 1.0), strings by value.
- `pyFloatRepr(x)` — JS number → CPython `repr(float)` string. Rules: `Infinity`→`'inf'`, `-Infinity`→`'-inf'`, `NaN`→`'nan'`, `0`→`'0.0'`, `-0`→`'-0.0'`. Get shortest round-trip digits via `x.toExponential()` (no argument, e.g. `(1.5e-7).toExponential()` → `'1.5e-7'`); parse sign, digit string, scientific exponent P. Python uses SCIENTIFIC notation when `P >= 16` or `P < -4`, else fixed. Fixed: plain decimal; if the value is integral append `.0` (e.g. `3` → `'3.0'`, `1000000000000000` → `'1000000000000000.0'`). Scientific: mantissa is first digit, then `.` + remaining digits ONLY if there is more than one digit (so `1e16` → `'1e+16'`, NOT `'1.0e+16'`; `1.5e-7` → `'1.5e-07'`); exponent always has a sign and at least 2 digits (`e+16`, `e-05`, `e-07`). Verified examples: `0.1`→`'0.1'`, `2.5`→`'2.5'`, `1e16`→`'1e+16'`, `1e17`→`'1e+17'`, `0.00001`→`'1e-05'`, `0.0001`→`'0.0001'`, `1.5e-7`→`'1.5e-07'`.
- `pyRepr(v)` — full Python `repr()`: `PyFloat`→pyFloatRepr of value; JS number (always a Python int in this model)→`String(v)` (booleans are separate); boolean→`'True'`/`'False'`; `null`/`undefined`→`'None'`; string→Python str repr (see below); JS array→list `'[a, b]'`; `PyTuple`→`'(a, b)'` (single element gets trailing comma `'(a,)'`, empty `'()'`); `PyDict`→`'{k: v, ...}'` (empty `'{}'`); any object with a `__pyRepr__()` method→call it (used by OMD/FrozenDict). Elements joined with `', '`.
